title: Authorization invalidation vectors v1
description:
One case per change that moves an authorization input, recording which surfaces it reaches and which derived artifacts it destroys. packages/schemas/projection-authorization-v1.json is the rule; this is the corpus it is measured on. scripts/repository/validate_planning_artifacts.py#evaluate_invalidation reaches every field of `expected` from the profile rather than reading it back, so a case whose recorded answer is wrong fails and the corpus cannot confirm itself.

The distinction the corpus exists to make is the one SR-015 turns on. A block, a board removal and a deletion each change what a live surface may render. None of them changes what a sealed ranking generation contains, and one of them — the deletion — is the only one that reaches an export download grant, because an export's subject and viewer are the same person. A corpus in which every trigger invalidated everything would prove nothing, which is why every case records what it retains as well as what it destroys.

unaffected_surfaces.description: Recorded rather than left implicit. A trigger that reached every surface and a trigger nobody worked out the blast radius of produce the same file when only the affected half is written down.

retained_artifacts.description: May be empty as a shape. Whether a corpus in which nothing survives any trigger is admissible is decided by the profile-level check in scripts/repository/validate_planning_artifacts.py, which refuses one where no perishable artifact is retained by any case and one where no artifact is authorization-independent. A minItems here would answer that question in the wrong file and would answer it less well: it would be satisfied by one case retaining one thing.
